title: Heterogeneous GPU probe cache and runtime compatibility layer
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem:
Our runtime currently probes device capabilities at cold-start on every host which is slow and brittle across mixed environments (MIG vs full-GPU, different CUDA versions, MPS enabled, NVLink topologies, and vendor driver minor versions). This leads to longer cold-start latency, duplicated probing work across containers, and surprising fallbacks when kernel ABI or quant kernels are not available.

Goal:
Create a lightweight, crash-tolerant probe cache and compatibility abstraction that: 
- Aggregates device capability fingerprints (compute capability, MIG partitions, MPS availability, driver minor) and available kernel feature sets (CUTLASS variants, Triton plugin versions, quantized kernel availability).
- Exposes a deterministic compatibility policy and quick fallback mapping from requested model/quant/profile -> compatible kernel artifact.
- Persists probe results to a secure local cache (on host) and provides a fast in-memory read cache in the runtime to avoid repeated heavy probing.
- Ships with safe invalidation heuristics (driver upgrade, kernel mismatch) and an opt-out for ephemeral containers.

Scope / Deliverables:
1) Probe cache library (C++/Rust): collect fingerprint + kernel registry lookup + local on-disk cache with TTL and safe tombstones.
2) Compatibility mapping service inside the runtime: policy evaluator that chooses kernel bundles using prioritized rules (exact match -> ABI-compatible substitution -> quantized fallback -> CPU fallback).
3) Migration path: feature flag to enable new probe cache, gradual rollout on dedicated clusters, fallback to old probing for edge cases.
4) Large-device test matrix and CI jobs exercising MIG partitions, MPS on/off, and driver rollback scenarios.
5) Benchmarks showing cold-start reduction and memory/CPU overhead.

Success criteria:
- Cold-start device probe time reduced by >= 60% in our standard e2e benchmark across 8 representative images.
- No increase in token-latency P50 for steady-state inference (<5% regression allowed).
- Zero customer-impact incidents during canary in dedicated pools (tracked by rollout dashboard).

Risks and mitigations:
- Inaccurate caching after driver upgrade -> mitigation: on-driver-version-mismatch invalidate cache immediately and re-probe; ship a strict tombstone TTL of 6 hours and an admin-triggered eviction.
- Security concerns around host-level cache -> mitigation: store only non-sensitive fingerprints, restrict file permissions to runtime user, and support optional encryption via KMS for private deployments.
- Compatibility complexity explosion -> mitigation: start with a simple prioritized rule engine and cover common cases first (CUTLASS quant kernels, Triton plugin ABI), deferring full policy DSL for follow-up.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: prototype probe cache library + unit tests.
- Week 2: integrate policy evaluator into runtime dev branch; initial e2e smoke tests.
- Week 3: internal canary on staging dedicated pool (feature flag).
- Week 4: iterate on failures, expand to 25% of dedicated capacity, run canary suite; create migration docs for Private customers.

Docs/Artifacts:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/PROBE-CACHE-2026 (internal)
- Initial benchmark results (prototype): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/drive-probe-cache-2026 (internal)
